pc88:190073.title: Kuronekosou Souzoku Satsujin Jiken

pc88:190075.description: Guide Vickey across question-mark tiles in each action-puzzle stage, collecting temporary powers while avoiding enemies.
pc88:190075.title: Laptick

pc88:190076.description: A PC-88 science-fiction mystery adventure with a spacecraft setting.
pc88:190076.title: Last Target

pc88:190077.description: Play futuristic pool on oddly shaped tables in solo or two-player matches.

pc88:190085.description: Create characters and lead a party of up to four on a fantasy role-playing journey.
pc88:190085.title: Majuu Senki Guardian

pc88:190088.description: A two-player turn-based war strategy game on a 41-by-41 square map.
pc88:190088.title: Morita no Battle Field

pc88:190089.title: Motoko-hime Adventure

pc88:190090.title: Mr. Bump

pc88:190092.title: Mystery House (Micro Cabin)

pc88:190093.description: An action role-playing game in ancient Egypt: Kaoru Jinguu, born into a family of shrine priests, fights with psychic power that grows in the world of myth.
pc88:190093.title: Necropolis

pc88:190094.description: A baseball management game by the later creator of Derby Stallion: manage a team through a 130-game pennant race and follow the batting and home-run races in detailed player statistics.

pc88:190095.description: Chunsoft's action game: Ron-kun collects all the fruit on each stage while avoiding enemies.
pc88:190095.title: Newtron

pc88:190096.description: Brain Grey's ninja role-playing game: three heroes, Jakimaru, Gen'yousai and Koheita, each pursue their own story while the others' stories advance alongside and cross it, and every ten days they can meet at a mountain hut to ask each other for help.

pc88:190719.title: Marvelous

pc88:190720.description: A role-playing game in the American West of 1853: young Jimmy sets out to become the biggest man in South Dakota by mining gold, catching outlaws and talking his way to a fortune.
pc88:190720.title: Seibu no Nariagari

pc88:193372.description: A riichi mahjong game based on Masayuki Katayama's manga Gambler Jiko Chuushinha.

pc88:193373.description: The second Gambler Jiko Chuushinha: mahjong against twelve more characters on an automatic table, with an octopus-hunting mode.

pc88:193374.description: The third Gambler Jiko Chuushinha: ten more characters, 34 in all with the first two games, and a new villain who wants to fill Japan with octopuses.

pc88:193375.description: A tile-matching puzzle in the manner of Shanghai, with tiles that flip face up when the tiles around them are taken, and advice from the series' characters when you're stuck.

pc88:193376.description: An action puzzle game: Gruppe rescues his friend Pasta.
pc88:193376.title: Gruppe

pc88:193377.description: An action game: Gutchan and Marichan go around town collecting money.

pc88:193379.description: Hudson's hanafuda card game with three styles of play, including koi-koi.
pc88:193379.title: Hanafuda Kyou

pc88:207594.description: A strategy simulation of aerial dogfights: choose from more than ten fighter types, such as the Zero and the Raiden, and play out a variety of air-combat engagements.
pc88:207594.title: Sky Tactics

aliases: Sorcerian System New Scenario: Uchuu kara no Houmonsha
pc88:207595.description: Extra scenarios for Sorcerian made by TAKERU: four new adventures by sea, through forests and out into space, and the magic shop WIZ selling new spells such as Flame and Corona.
pc88:207595.title: Sorcerian New Scenario: Uchuu kara no Houmonsha

pc88:207596.description: Falcom's first scenario disk for Sorcerian, with five adventures: The Devil's Island, The Temple of Sacrifice, The Bride Bewitched by the Devil, Ah, Where Is Josephine Now, and The Amazon's Sword.
pc88:207596.title: Sorcerian System Scenario Vol. 1

aliases: Sorcerian Tsuika Scenario Vol. 2: Sengoku Sorcerian
pc88:207597.description: Sengoku Sorcerian, Falcom's second scenario disk: five linked level-5 adventures set in Japan's Warring States period, played in order, with warlords such as Takeda Shingen and Oda Nobunaga and an ending of its own.
pc88:207597.title: Sorcerian System Scenario Vol. 2

aliases: Sorcerian Tsuika Scenario Vol. 3: Pyramid Sorcerian
pc88:207598.description: Pyramid Sorcerian, Falcom's third scenario disk: defeat Gilbares, the great demon lord behind Sengoku Sorcerian, in a pyramid full of traps and riddles.
pc88:207598.title: Sorcerian System Scenario Vol. 3: Pyramid Sorcerian

pc88:207599.description: The original Sokoban: push crates onto their marked spots in a warehouse, never pulling.
pc88:207599.title: Soko-Ban

pc88:207600.description: The second Sokoban, with fifty new warehouse puzzles.
pc88:207600.title: Soko-Ban 2

pc88:207601.description: Sokoban: push crates onto their marked spots in a warehouse, never pulling, across many puzzles.
pc88:207601.title: Perfect Soko-ban

pc88:207602.description: A fixed-screen shooter: from your fighter at the bottom of the screen, blast an evil space amoeba and the swarm of spawn it sends down at you.
pc88:207602.title: Space Amoeba

pc88:207604.description: The second Starlight Adventure, continuing the sci-fi text adventure.
pc88:207604.title: Starlight Adventure: Part 2

pc88:207605.description: A turn-based sci-fi strategy game: command a moon base against an unknown enemy.
pc88:207605.title: Storm: Neo Strategic Simulation

pc88:207606.description: A text adventure about a little mother mouse in need.
pc88:207606.title: The Stray Story

pc88:207607.description: An action role-playing game: the demon lord Pay Valusa invades the peaceful island of Rwanda.
pc88:207607.title: Tritorn

pc88:207608.description: A side-scrolling action role-playing game: the demon Geld sends his army against humanity again.
pc88:207608.title: Tritorn II: Road of Darkness

pc88:207609.description: A card game collection with five games: concentration, gin rummy, speed, blackjack and poker, drawn with detailed card graphics.
pc88:207609.title: Trump Kyou

pc88:207610.description: A collection of 120 tsumego, Go life-and-death puzzles.
pc88:207610.title: Tsumego 120

pc88:207612.description: A prize winner in Enix's first contest: shoot enemies in four directions in space, floating against a gravity that pulls you down.
pc88:207612.title: Uchuu no Senshi

pc88:207616.description: A baseball simulation played from the manager's chair, building on Xtal Soft's Mr. Pro Yakyuu: pick one of 13 teams, the 12 pro clubs or one of your own, run spring camp with a focus on stamina, mental strength or fielding, then set each day's schedule through the pennant race. Player data goes as far as birth month and stress.
pc88:207616.title: Yakyuu Dou: The Way to Gloria

pc88:207617.description: An upgraded version of the baseball management simulation Yakyuu Dou with far more detailed data: team editing down to the undershirts, practice menus covering fitness and mindset, advance talks with draft picks and foreign players, and a ronin mode that lets you keep playing after being fired for poor results.
pc88:207617.title: Yakyuu Dou II

aliases: Zenkoku Nanpa Shugyou: Tasogare no Kyouto hen
pc88:207620.description: A pick-up game set in twilight Kyoto: you try to chat up women by answering the three quiz questions shown on each screen, advancing with right answers, while too many misses eventually end the game.
pc88:207620.title: Zenkoku Nanpa Shugyou: Tasogare no Kyoto Hen

pc88:207621.description: Guide a robot through the computer city Zenon to destroy its runaway central core. The robot fires beams in four directions and can hide behind the scrolling terrain, such as gutters, to avoid attacks.
pc88:207621.title: Computer City Zenon

pc88:207622.description: A fixed-screen pseudo-3D shooter in the style of Gyruss.
pc88:207622.title: Zexas

pc88:207632.description: An action game: steer a fan to blow four balls into the warehouse.
pc88:207632.title: Fan Fun

pc88:207633.description: Two games in one: The Racer, a 3D Formula One race kept fast by a bare background, and the vertical shooter Galaxy Fighter.
pc88:207633.title: The Racer & Galaxy Fighter

pc88:207636.description: An action maze game: a thousand years ago, aliens invade the city of Kyo, and a guardsman digs pits to trap them.
pc88:207636.title: Heiankyo Alien

pc88:207639.description: Koei's first war simulation, based on the battles of Kawanakajima.
pc88:207639.title: Kawanakajima no Kassen

pc88:207640.description: Koei's fantasy role-playing game: an evil wizard has killed the benevolent king of Border Land.
pc88:207640.title: Ken to Mahou

pc88:207642.description: One of Koei's first games, written by Kou Shibusawa: command twenty German divisions against the 1944 Allied landings, short of men, supplies and morale, and hold Paris for a month or wear the Allies down.
pc88:207642.title: Normandy Jouriku Sakusen

pc88:207648.description: A side-scrolling shooter: fly over mountainous terrain, bombing and shooting your way to the enemy base.
pc88:207648.title: Scramble

pc88:207650.description: A fantasy role-playing game: explore dangerous wilderness to find a legendary sword.
pc88:207650.title: Seiken Densetsu

pc88:207653.description: A space battle game in the tradition of Star Trek: find thirty enemy ships with long-range sensors, set their 3D coordinates in the autopilot, then line them up by hand and fire.
pc88:207653.title: Star Fleet

pc88:207655.description: A war simulation of the Battle of the Java Sea: command the Japanese fleet against the Allied squadron.
pc88:207655.title: Surabaya-oki Kaisen

pc88:207656.description: A tank game in the style of the arcade Tank Battalion: your one tank defends headquarters against the enemy's last counterattack, and destroying twenty tanks clears a stage.
pc88:207656.title: Tank Batabata

pc88:207658.description: A text adventure: adrift in the Pacific after a shipwreck, you come upon a sailing ship from the Age of Discovery and its secret.
pc88:207658.title: Yuureisen

pc88:207703.description: A war strategy game: play Miss Serizawa, a brilliant and unhinged scientist who arrives on a giant tanker to invade her own homeland, the Empire of Japan.
pc88:207703.title: G Senryaku

pc88:207715.description: A monochrome illustrated text adventure set in a Victorian mansion where the guests are being murdered.
pc88:207715.title: Mystery House (StarCraft)

pc88:207718.description: A science-fiction role-playing game starring characters by manga artist Tou Moriyama: you must escape the clutches of an enemy who wants to make you his slave.
pc88:207718.title: Toraware Penguin

aliases: Mobile Suit Gundam: Luna Tsu no Tatakai
Mobile Suit Gundam: Luna Tsū no Tatakai

pc88:207839.title: Mobile Suit Gundam: Luna 2 no Tatakai

pc88:207896.description: Hudson's original Bomberman: lay bombs to clear walls and destroy enemies in a maze.
pc88:207896.title: Bomber Man

pc88:207898.description: A top-down racing game based on the film Cannonball Run II.
pc88:207898.title: Cannon Ball 2

pc88:207904.description: A gambling game: bet with a demon on where his roulette ball will land.
pc88:207904.title: Demon Roulette

pc88:207909.description: A space shooter starring the Cosmo Fighter Jestar.
pc88:207909.title: Galactron

pc88:207910.description: Hudson's 3D golf game, with the golfer drawn in wireframe.
pc88:207910.title: Golf Kyou

pc88:207911.description: A single-screen platformer: a cat-like hero collects every apple on each level.
pc88:207911.title: Harvest

pc88:207912.description: A 3D tank combat game: destroy as many enemy tanks and mines as you can.
pc88:207912.title: Hiroton Wars

pc88:207917.description: A koi-koi hanafuda game on a wide field; leave a card unplayed for 30 seconds and the computer plays it for you.
pc88:207917.title: Koi Koi

pc88:207918.description: A shooting game: your robot fires beams left and right at attacking enemies and refuels at a docking station that passes below.
pc88:207918.title: MJ-05

pc88:207919.description: Move through a bright garden maze in this Enix action game.
pc88:207919.title: Magic Garden

pc88:207920.description: A text adventure: Princess Seiko has been abducted by the witch Moheka.
pc88:207920.title: Majo Moheka no Yakata

pc88:207921.description: An adventure: a section manager pursues an office romance with a 23-year-old colleague during the lunch hour from 12:00 to 1:10.
pc88:207921.title: Office Love no Tehodoki: Lunch Time Hen

pc88:207923.description: An action shooter set in a land loosely based on the anime Aura Battler Dunbine.
pc88:207923.title: Outer Land

pc88:207924.description: An early 3D shooter: blast the enemy fighters pouring from the distance on the long flight to the enemy fortress rising over the horizon.
pc88:207924.title: Polar Star III

pc88:207925.description: Koei's early adventure with role-playing combat: rescue a princess carried off by a dragon.
pc88:207925.title: Dragon & Princess

pc88:207926.description: Micro Cabin's golf game over nine holes.
pc88:207926.title: The Golf

pc88:207928.description: An action game: a monkey drops blocks to defeat PIRAN, a strange fish.
pc88:207928.title: Utan Jr.

pc88:207957.description: A pinball game with true-to-life ball motion and simple rules, where bonuses, bumpers and gravity can be adjusted.
pc88:207957.title: Super Pinball

pc88:208641.description: A spy infiltration story inspired by Mission: Impossible, set in a mechanized nuclear reactor complex.
pc88:208641.title: Mission Impossible

pc88:209127.description: A Votoms side story: Sergeant Macoleen, sole known survivor of the elite Black Unicorn unit, is sent alone into a crashed super carrier held by rebels, fighting armored troopers through its thirty maze-like decks.
pc88:209127.title: Votoms Black Unicorn

pc88:209128.description: A behind-view shooter against the space invaders Golgoda.
pc88:209128.title: Red Stack!

pc88:218376.description: An Urusei Yatsura game adapted from the anime episode in which Lum creates a special lipstick.
pc88:218376.title: Urusei Yatsura: Rouge Magic

pc88:218379.description: An Urusei Yatsura game: collect ten dotted flowers while avoiding cats and poisoned mushrooms.
pc88:218379.title: Urusei Yatsura: Himitsu no Hanazono

pc88:424143.description: Daifugo, the Japanese climbing card game.
pc88:424143.title: Kyan Kyan Collection

pc88:424147.description: A command-driven adventure following a schoolgirl, Kanako, and her friend: Look and Talk carry most scenes, other actions appear when a scene calls for them, and a few optional scenes and routes branch off the story.
pc88:424147.title: Assorted Friendship

pc88:440282.description: An adventure: a young man follows the trail of his abducted girlfriend Alisa.
pc88:440282.title: Teiō no Yabō

pc88:440284.title: Cybernetic Hi-School Part 3: Gunbuster

pc88:442243.description: A memory game: follow the five tones of the memory machine and key in the flashing numbers to sharpen the picture, over twelve stages.
pc88:442243.title: Karei Naru Er♥chikku Memorī

pc88:453654.description: A cross between a tile-based adventure and a shooter: steer your spaceship around a grid map collecting upgrades, then take on bosses that each surrender a valuable item when beaten.
pc88:453654.title: Berserkers Front Gaiden 3

pc88:453667.description: The last Magnet World puzzle-platformer: Magnet Girl clears each stage by bringing opposite-pole magnets together to destroy them, also using magnets as steps and lifts. Adds three difficulty levels, a stage editor, background art and indestructible container boxes that push matching magnets upward.
pc88:453667.title: Magnet World Final

pc88:453668.description: The harder sequel to Magnet World: a doujin puzzle platformer.
pc88:453668.title: Magnet World 2

pc88:453669.description: A puzzle game: knock over matching colored pins with balls.
pc88:453669.title: Pazrun

pc88:456634.title: Sisty Lier: The Adventure of Salia

pc88:456637.description: A side story to Suiryuushi: the harpist Pantelro and Medi of the sea folk explore a village whose mermaids have stopped answering; first a bonus mini-game with the PC-98 Suiryuushi II, expanded into a full game.
pc88:456637.title: Suiryuushi Bangaihen: Mediflora no Izumi

pc88:456641.description: An adventure: you are the spirit in a red stone, unable to move, who can possess whoever holds it and learn what they know.
pc88:456641.title: Evil Stone

pc88:456647.description: A doujin fantasy adventure made for the PC-88 by the circle Ramble Dots, following the boy Fel and the girl Timny as they travel an RPG-style 2D map. It supports the Sound Board II.
pc88:456647.title: Tiny Troubadour: Dark Shrine

pc88:456663.description: A comedy adventure in the Edo period: a swordswoman at a detective agency is hired to carry a small box of documents to a clan's castle, and the errand becomes a long adventure.
pc88:456663.title: Tsuukai Gag Aventure: Narutomaki Hichou

pc88:456667.description: A yes-or-no trivia quiz: questions on all kinds of subjects appear one after another and must be answered within a time limit, with each correct answer uncovering more of a picture by artist Wataru Watanabe. The questions are surprisingly hard.
pc88:456667.title: Zatsugaku Olympics: Watanabe Wataru-hen

pc88:456735.description: A blend of adventure and role-playing without experience levels: set out to recover the stolen snow crystal and defeat the evil spirit Deldgordon to restore peace to the northern land of Cluju.
pc88:456735.title: Cluju

pc88:456737.title: Mahou no Shinigami Lali Lalii Ahena

pc88:457562.description: A vertically scrolling shooter with no story: starting from level 0, shoot down incoming craft, some of which drop power-ups for faster autofire, extra shots or repairs, and face a boss at the end of every level.
pc88:457562.title: Hard Rank

pc88:457689.description: A doujin Sokoban-style game: guide Kana as she pushes balls into holes.
pc88:457689.title: Puzzle Kana?

pc88:457973.description: A platform game: climb ladders to reach the top floor of each stage.
pc88:457973.title: Ascend

pc88:457979.description: A fantasy game: the fairies of Ever Green have been turned into monsters that are changing the land.
pc88:457979.title: Ever Green

pc88:457984.description: An adventure in which the legendary mercenary Jamie Star travels to Shanghai at the height of the Cold War to recover a client's cargo, amid conspiracies and the city's underworld.
pc88:457984.title: Shanghai (1985)

pc88:457988.description: A doujin Tetris-style puzzle game with three modes.
pc88:457988.title: Tetras

pc88:457989.description: The Rally-X sequel: drive through the maze collecting flags while dodging pursuing cars.
pc88:457989.title: New Rally-X

pc88:458271.description: A platformer: as a cat burglar, steal every painting from each level while avoiding the guards.
pc88:458271.title: The Heist

pc88:459602.description: A memory game: study an illustration, then judge whether each sixth of a picture you're shown matches it.
pc88:459602.title: Breeze

pc88:459605.description: The Mole Mole sequel, a Boulder Dash-like puzzle platformer.
pc88:459605.title: Mole Mole 2

pc88:459606.description: A role-playing adventure from the radio show Miyake Yuji's Young Paradise: collect the Hiranya and other items to find the ultimate Hiranya power, moving around a map and talking to people.
pc88:459606.title: Yanpara Adventure: Hiranya no Nazo

pc88:459612.description: An action role-playing game: thrown into the Sengoku era by a time-machine accident, Hayato searches for his lost girlfriend Liza, infiltrates the Hidden Edo Castle and defeats the Dark Shogun, over four chapters.
pc88:459612.title: Hayato

pc88:460365.description: Falcom's golf game over nine holes.
pc88:460365.title: Computer the Golf

pc88:461887.description: PSK's first L♥lita game: rock-paper-scissors against a young girl; win too fast and the police arrest you.
pc88:461887.title: L♥lita

pc88:462003.description: Two years after the first game, Ria is packed off by her wizard master to rescue the eastern kingdom, whose king has fallen under the control of an evil sorcerer. Played as a "computer comic": the story runs with few prompts, each command is one word, usually a spell, and it adds animated scenes.
pc88:462003.title: Mahoutsukai no Deshi II: Tougoku no Sisha

pc88:462156.description: An action game: the puppy Muku delivers the mail through 100 towns laid out like mazes, pushing blue walls to clear the way without blocking it.
pc88:462156.title: Muku no Yuubinyasan

pc88:462176.description: A platformer: a ninja collects treasures while avoiding patrolling guards.
pc88:462176.title: Ninja-kun

pc88:462189.description: A self-parody of Nukenin Densetsu: Gyuutarou, son of the first game's ox-masked foe, seeks revenge on Jakimaru with two ox-headed companions; sold only to members of the game's user club.
pc88:462189.title: Nukenin Densetsu Bangai-hen

pc88:462237.description: An action game: You-chan, a part-time painter, paints her way through each stage.
pc88:462237.title: Penki-ya You-chan

pc88:462244.description: Koei's two-player baseball game: pick teams and starting lineups from the stars of the twelve professional clubs.
pc88:462244.title: Pennant Race

pc88:462292.description: A tongue-in-cheek puzzle game parodying 1980s computer manga.
pc88:462292.title: Panga

pc88:462297.description: A star-chart program, the follow-up to Champion Soft's The Planetarium: it shows the night sky turning as time passes, and lets you set the viewing location, date, time and direction freely.
pc88:462297.title: Orion: Planetarium Part II

aliases: ポンコツ船サバイバル
pc88:462298.description: An action game: captain a battered ship across a long, dangerous voyage.
pc88:462298.title: Ponkotsu-sen Survival

pc88:462318.description: A power-up disk for Pro Yakyuu Fan: choose starting lineups, create original teams, make trades and play against Telenet's own team.
pc88:462318.title: Pro Yakyuu Fan: Power Up Kit - Yousei Gips

aliases: プロフェッショナル麻雀
pc88:462344.title: Professional Mahjong

aliases: 連合艦隊の栄光 栗田艦隊レイテ湾突入
pc88:462404.description: A war simulation of the Battle of Leyte Gulf near the end of World War II, with four fleets in distinct roles for complex operations.
pc88:462404.title: Rengo Kantai no Eiko: Kurita Kantai Rei de wan Totsunyuu

pc88:462417.description: An adventure at a school: Sachi loves 500-yen coins, and the hero hunts for a rare one among the schoolgirls.
pc88:462417.title: Sacchan no Daibouken

aliases: Saotome Military Academy of U.N. Space Force
pc88:462447.description: An adventure set at the Military Academy of the U.N. Space Force, a women-only school that trains its students to pilot mecha.
pc88:462447.title: Kokuren Uchuu Gun Shikan Gakkou: Saotome Gakuen Nyuugaku Annai

aliases: サミー・ライトフット
pc88:462448.description: Sierra's platformer: jump obstacles across three levels using trampolines and swings.
pc88:462448.title: Sammy Lightfoot

pc88:462513.description: A celebrated 3D action game by Tainyan: explore a vast maze at high speed in Game A or race the clock in Game B, drawn so fast that it puts the floppy drive's own processor to work.
pc88:462513.title: SeeNa

pc88:462536.description: A wargame of nine famous battles fought by Second World War generals and Sengoku-era commanders, including Rommel at El Alamein, Patton at the Bulge and Sekigahara. The enemy moves first on the main map, then you; units that meet switch to a battle mode, orders are limited to move and scout, and there is no retreating once a fight begins.
pc88:462536.title: Senjou no Hoshi

aliases: Shiro to Kuro no Densetsu Series Joukan: Destruction
pc88:462679.description: The first part of Destruction: a TV broadcast is interrupted by a voice saying to look at the midnight sky.
pc88:462679.title: Destruction Joukan

pc88:464628.description: A CD bundled with the PC-8801MC, with rolling and playable demos of games such as Misty Blue and Thexder.
pc88:464628.title: CD Takarabako

pc88:465705.description: A Qix-style game of claiming territory to reveal a picture.
pc88:465705.title: Shampoo

pc88:465933.description: A shogi game on a carved-wood board: tell the computer which opening to play, such as Sanken Bisha or Yagura, and save and load game records.
pc88:465933.title: Shogi 88

pc88:465939.description: ASCII's shogi game, known for its strength and quick moves, with replay, game records and take-backs.
pc88:465939.title: Shogi

aliases: スーパーベースボール
pc88:466555.title: Super Baseball

pc88:local-002b805ee8.description: A doujin horizontal shooter that has nothing to do with Konami's own sequel and plays more like the first Salamander: power up a small ship by destroying enemies, clear the screen with a limited stock of wipers that enemies can replenish, and beat a boss at the end of every stage.
pc88:local-002b805ee8.title: Salamander II

pc88:local-00added768.description: The last PC-88 release from Ayashige Soft, a cheap Sound Board II music disk whose draw was a recreation of the opening of Capcom's arcade Vampire (Darkstalkers), rendered in single-color text graphics.
pc88:local-00added768.title: Vampire BGM Shuu

pc88:local-00c28a9a32.description: A collection of Junichi Ueda's famously accurate arcade transcriptions, first written for the X68000's MXDRV and ported to the PC-88 by the MDRV driver's author: over 20 tracks from Galaxy Force, Ordyne, Thunder Cross, Power Drift, Metal Hawk, Super Hang-On, Sorcerian and more.
pc88:local-00c28a9a32.title: Ueda Junichi BGM Collection Vol. 1

pc88:local-014f982311.description: A doujin variation on Missile Command that defends one huge city: aim a big cursor to shoot down falling missiles and mushroom-shaped spacecraft, with up to three hyper bombs that wipe out everything on screen.
pc88:local-014f982311.title: Missile Panic

pc88:local-0199b77650.description: A doujin parody of R-Type: a horizontal shooter where destroyed enemies drop stronger shots, bombs, shields and extra screen-clearing wipers, and every stage ends with a boss that needs its own tactic.
pc88:local-0199b77650.title: Y-Type Special

pc88:local-01ea13635f.description: A memory game: ESP-style cards marked with a circle, triangle, square, cross or plus flash briefly at the top of the screen and must be called back; display time depends on the level, more cards appear as stages advance, and digitized pictures serve as the reward.
pc88:local-01ea13635f.title: Nugi Nugi Eawase Speed

pc88:local-02170816c9.description: Active Gamers' second command-based RPG, subtitled Shinjitsu no Megami-hen, released in 1992 on four disks with a larger scenario and better graphics and music than the first Holiness Story; a preview demo disk went to mail-order buyers.
pc88:local-02170816c9.title: Holiness Story II

pc88:local-0389e327a3.description: The first music disk from the Orphe circle (1991) for the Sound Board II: mostly original tunes by YAMA, RIU and KIN plus arrangements from Ys, Castlevania, Gradius III and Lightning Fighters, with drums played on the YM2608's rhythm sounds instead of PCM samples.
pc88:local-0389e327a3.title: Orphe Music Disk

pc88:local-0427d8a222.description: A doujin Columns clone: drop stacks of three tiles to line up three or more of the same tile, with bombs that clear every tile of one kind.
pc88:local-0427d8a222.title: Kramus

pc88:local-04b5aff68d.description: An NT-3 music disk from Active Gamers (1994) with 51 tracks mixing NT-3's own pieces and game music covers, ranging from F-Zero's Mute City to Sailor Moon's Moonlight Densetsu; it came out for both the PC-88 and PC-98.
pc88:local-04b5aff68d.title: Propensity - NT-3 Music Disk

pc88:local-055173be69.description: A free bonus disk that came with Firecracker's volume 13: 58 rejected tracks mixing game music with TM Network songs, music from Maison Ikkoku and the NHK news theme, played back without a track selection mode.
pc88:local-055173be69.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 14 - Return of Botsu Music

pc88:local-0576e20a05.description: An apology disk from Hoehoe Team 199X that offers background music from Chousenshi Hoehoe 3, a game the circle never managed to release.
pc88:local-0576e20a05.title: Chousenshi Hoehoe 3 ga Dekinakute Gomen no Disk

pc88:local-060ccd66ef.description: KOB Soft's follow-up to Rinse, keeping its reverse-Othello rules but with harder stages and new opponents modeled on a famous team of moon-themed girl warriors.
pc88:local-060ccd66ef.title: Moon Rinse

pc88:local-0636fc95f2.description: Onion Software's 1988 3D space-shooting RPG about a priest who roams the galaxy spreading his faith from planet to planet, meeting strange aliens and objects on the way to a tower dungeon on a blue planet; two disks with many graphics and over 50 music tracks.
pc88:local-0636fc95f2.title: The Airrector

pc88:local-0814190fa5.description: A late Firecracker music disk whose title screen puts Hatsune Miku in front of characters from Cheetahmen II, and whose tracks include music from Cheetahmen II.
pc88:local-0814190fa5.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 37 - Electrospective Harmony

pc88:local-099623a790.description: A role-playing game that began as doujin software: in 2020, two superpowers on the brink of ruin from military spending turn to force to win back their place, with auto-mapping and a cockpit view.
pc88:local-099623a790.title: Operation L

pc88:local-09c5dd8711.description: The sequel to Mature: as a heart, push blocks so the young woman who wanders on her own reaches the door.
pc88:local-09c5dd8711.title: Mature II

pc88:local-0a45596da2.description: Frostforest's second sample music disk (1992), a Final Fantasy IV special, which introduced an on-screen keyboard display, a compressed kanji routine supporting rare characters, and a serialized comic story by the staff.
pc88:local-0a45596da2.title: FSD Sample Ongaku Shuu Vol. 2

pc88:local-0ac52c023b.description: The third and final Imagical Musion Depot (1996), a two-disk Active Gamers anthology of 35 mostly original FM tracks by NT-3, Monden, OSATOH, yon, Anima and other doujin musicians, made for the Takeru software vending machines.
pc88:local-0ac52c023b.title: Imagical Musion Depot Vol. 3

pc88:local-0b960eecd2.description: The fourth 100 Yen Disk (1988) and the only two-disk one, packed with odd games: The Quest of Orclot with cute characters, the Fa-Fa Game of handing money to a bear cub, a strawberry-juice game, a cockroach-swatting game and Haruma Game, a peek at a day in a game studio.
pc88:local-0b960eecd2.title: 100 Yen Disk No. 4

pc88:local-0bd7373e65.description: Shogi lessons: the computer plays out a game and, at key moments, asks you to pick the next move from four, then shows what follows from your choice.
pc88:local-0bd7373e65.title: The Shogi Juku

pc88:local-0cf00e1ddd.description: A 1988 quiz styled on the Attack Chance of the TV show Panel Quiz Attack 25: correct answers flip panels to uncover pictures of 40 girls, and the absurdly long full title parodies the Narita Airport rock-paper-scissors round of America Oudan Ultra Quiz.
pc88:local-0cf00e1ddd.title: Hard-sha no Shachou ga...

pc88:local-0d0ddcbb25.description: Lotus Roots' puzzle platformer, a renamed Magnet Girl: a girl in a magnet suit switches between red and blue to push magnets into ones of opposite polarity to destroy them, using magnets as stairs and lifts.
pc88:local-0d0ddcbb25.title: Magnet World

pc88:local-0d23867040.description: Xtalsoft's music collection of tracks from its own games.
pc88:local-0d23867040.title: Digital Jukebox

pc88:local-0d39a20fcb.description: Pastel Software's Ys-themed board game: roll the die to reach the house in the top-left corner, making decisions on some spaces while others end the game at once, as can rolling a minus one at the start.
pc88:local-0d39a20fcb.title: Ganbare! Adol-kun!! - Minimini Ys

pc88:local-0db2f5521e.description: A simulation: as a member of the earthquake prediction committee, read geological data to forecast when the big one will strike and keep the economic damage down.
pc88:local-0db2f5521e.title: Kyodai Jishin

pc88:local-0e22a78160.description: A visual novel in which a girl whose mother is bedridden sets out on a journey to find a cure for her illness.
pc88:local-0e22a78160.title: Cauliflower

pc88:local-0e4b94d561.description: The first 100 Yen Disk compilation: Shooting Master '86, an adventure that leads into a fixed-screen shooter; Graman Bee, a space shooter about blasting space worms for power-ups; an electronic novel; the Breakout imitation The Rotten Wall; and the one-life spike-jumping runner Jumpper.
pc88:local-0e4b94d561.title: 100 Yen Disk No. 1

pc88:local-0e6a890032.description: An Onion Software compilation disk mixing doujin games with CG, preview screens and game programming engines.
pc88:local-0e6a890032.title: Mazekko Disk

pc88:local-0e82ab1668.description: A CG collection disk of digital illustrations by HAGA-KEN, one of the best-known PC-88 doujin CG artists.
pc88:local-0e82ab1668.title: WGC - The Digital Trip Illustration

pc88:local-0f5d551e66.description: Active Gamers' third 100-yen disk magazine (1993), built around their RPG Undine with a corner covering the game, an Undine music mode and a collection of previously unreleased PC-88 music.
pc88:local-0f5d551e66.title: Extra Disk Vol. 3

pc88:local-112861eb52.description: A quiz game: told by the king that he may wed the princess only by answering questions, the hero defeats the court officials one by one in quizzes; its current-events questions were already years old on release.
pc88:local-112861eb52.title: Princess Quest

pc88:local-11749f90fc.description: An unofficial fan port of Namco's Bosconian: fly through space destroying enemy battle stations by knocking out their outer cannons or hitting the core, while dodging fighters, missiles, meteors and mines and catching the escaping spy ship.
pc88:local-11749f90fc.title: Bosconian

pc88:local-119a248df5.description: A 2D wireframe battle game that won LOGiN's software contest and was sold through Brother's Takeru machines: in 989 New A.D. the giant creature Gavither returns with a huge meteor, and a newly found fighter must stop him for good.
pc88:local-119a248df5.title: Prodigy

pc88:local-11b5f6ebab.description: A quiz game by the SIVA collective with help from Burning Apple, Creative H.A.T., G.Create and SSG, where each girl has her own artist and quiz category, and music by Onion.
pc88:local-11b5f6ebab.title: Powerful Engine

pc88:local-11b609b080.description: One of five Firecracker music disks released together in 1990 for 200 yen each, covering video game music programmed in BASIC MML under ALPHA-mini DOS, which traded some sound quality for a large track count.
pc88:local-11b609b080.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 02 - Video Game Century

pc88:local-122aa09a3b.description: Firecracker's first-anniversary issue (1991), its fifteenth disk in a single year, adding livelier PCM loading screens, a handier track selector and staff credits that roll over the ending theme of Dragon Slayer: The Legend of Heroes.
pc88:local-122aa09a3b.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 15 - First Anniversary!!

pc88:local-1240ead271.description: A blackjack-like card game in which reaching 21 is not always best and going over is not always a loss, with three tries against each opponent.
pc88:local-1240ead271.title: Pop Card

pc88:local-1311ce2393.description: Burning Apple's sequel adventure with action elements, in which the hero leaves his body as a spirit; its artwork was later carried almost unchanged into the commercial Sweet Angel from Active.
pc88:local-1311ce2393.title: Sweet Girl 2 - Body Game

pc88:local-132a8f29e1.description: A doujin sequel to Bothtec's The Scheme, made quickly by the same staff and sold only once at Comiket: a brutally hard action game pairing Ys III-style side-scrolling with The Scheme's shooting, with a surreal streak of flying cows and Sound Board II music by Yuzo Koshiro.
pc88:local-132a8f29e1.title: Wanderers from Super Scheme

pc88:local-1369a7b8a9.title: Konya mo Makezu ni Powerful Ogeretsu Game

pc88:local-13a589ab10.description: A Ryokusui Sound Team music disk featuring a large selection of Dragon Quest III arrangements.
pc88:local-13a589ab10.title: RST Music Disk Vol. 04

pc88:local-14004dcb7f.description: A dungeon-crawling RPG: buy weapons, armor and a spell, then search a dungeon for pompoms, choosing to fight, cast or flee in random encounters.
pc88:local-14004dcb7f.title: Pon Pon Quest

pc88:local-14823964ad.description: The quietly released third episode of Amazing Disk, OSS's TRON Computer Diagnosis, which tells a story the player advances by answering yes or no.
pc88:local-14823964ad.title: Amazing Disk Episode III

pc88:local-149673c68b.description: A comic adventure that is really a minigame collection: otaku Arashi Tanaka travels to the end of the Edo period, where Ryoma Sakamoto kidnaps his time-machine-inventing relative, and must win minigames to recruit great figures from history, starting in ancient Egypt.
pc88:local-149673c68b.title: Ishin no Game Center Arashi

pc88:local-1511cfcadc.description: A Firecracker music disk made for Comiket 42 in August 1992, composed, arranged and programmed by CHEMOOL with PMD: doujin originals and arrangements from Tetraforce, Vapor Trail, Atomic Robo-Kid, Midnight Resistance, Dirt Fox and X68000 Bosconian, among others.
pc88:local-1511cfcadc.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. A - Comike 42 Special

pc88:local-15c6f60e07.description: A doujin horizontal shooter built as a near one-to-one copy of Irem's R-Type.
pc88:local-15c6f60e07.title: S-Type

pc88:local-163243cb20.description: ASCII's shogi game, with eight levels up to amateur first dan, tsume-shogi problems of up to fifteen moves, and printed game records.
pc88:local-163243cb20.title: Kisei

pc88:local-164b4123dd.description: Elein Soft's first software release (1987), after three earlier volumes appeared in print: as manga artist Miki Kawada, go out picking up girls in search of material for your work.
pc88:local-164b4123dd.title: New Loaders Vol. 4

pc88:local-1671cffd8e.description: Firecracker's 1990 music disk devoted to Konami SCC-chip tunes such as Gradius II and Parodius, with a PCM-voiced Chichibinta Rika theme as its centerpiece.
pc88:local-1671cffd8e.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 08 - Konami SCC Masterpieces

pc88:local-17219482a8.description: Probably the first doujin disk magazine, by BERO of Dennou Kagaku Kenkyuujo, promoter of the Pi image format: his columns plus playable trials of the circle's games, handed out at Pasoket events for the price of the disk.
pc88:local-17219482a8.title: Dennou Tsuushin Vol. 1

pc88:local-182d3714f8.description: Team TBL's Tetris clone with a normal mode, where clearing a set number of lines advances the level, and an endless mode played until all lives are lost, both speeding up as they go, plus a music mode.
pc88:local-182d3714f8.title: Tinker Bell 2

pc88:local-185de07406.description: LOGiN magazine's first original tool, introduced in its November 1986 issue: a PC-8801 kit for building your own Ultima-style overhead RPGs, often cited as a forerunner of RPG Tsukuru.
pc88:local-185de07406.title: RPG Construction

pc88:local-187ec06f9c.description: An adventure about Kimiko Suzuki, a first-year schoolgirl at St. Francisco Girls' School, who runs into her junior-high classmate Sakaguchi in a park.
pc88:local-187ec06f9c.title: Take Out Vol. 2

pc88:local-19cdf8546b.description: A top-down adventure in the style of Old Village Story: a young woman searches the Forest of No Return for her lover, who went exploring there, avoiding beasts and monsters with her wits rather than fighting.
pc88:local-19cdf8546b.title: Mahoroba

pc88:local-1a66f06041.title: Tanteidan X Bangaihen - Fushigi na Kanzume

pc88:local-1b30983a09.description: An adventure in which the hero finds a purse and must return it to the right person; wrong choices leave him empty-handed.
pc88:local-1b30983a09.title: Abunai Geimu

pc88:local-1b78077d6b.description: A 1991 Firecracker disk heavy on Dragon Saber and Dragon Spirit music, also featuring Actraiser with string PCM samples, picks from E.D.F. and Kengou, and original pieces by guest composers.
pc88:local-1b78077d6b.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 17 - Show Your Good Sounds!

pc88:local-1c07557f83.description: A card game played with mahjong-tile symbols: the player and the computer take turns placing cards, and each placement changes a map on the board.
pc88:local-1c07557f83.title: Bargon no Paka Paka Daibouken

pc88:local-1cc03f0f93.description: A placement puzzle in the spirit of the eight queens problem: put the randomly offered pieces where they match no piece in the same row or column by color or pattern until the quota is filled, with a help function and swappable data disks of other designs.
pc88:local-1cc03f0f93.title: Card Force IV

pc88:local-1cf6fbf91e.description: A 1985 adventure whose original story and script were written by science-fiction novelist Sakyo Komatsu; commands are chosen with the function keys and the player moves with the numeric keypad.
pc88:local-1cf6fbf91e.title: The Adventure of Blue Cosmos

pc88:local-1d1e69c4a3.description: The first Imagical Musion Depot (1994), a 35-track anthology that Active Gamers produced for the Takeru vending machines with well-known doujin musicians including NT-3, Monden, OSATOH, yon and Anima.
pc88:local-1d1e69c4a3.title: Imagical Musion Depot Vol. 1

pc88:local-1d66f03498.description: Released in 1993 after a year-long gap, this Firecracker disk covers four titles: Sword Dancer, the X68000's Little Chinese Final, Gravity Response and Variable Geo.
pc88:local-1d66f03498.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 29 - Battle Game Issue

pc88:local-1de468366b.description: A doujin RPG about a young man on an island who fights monsters and human enemies while buying better weapons and armor.
pc88:local-1de468366b.title: Jark

pc88:local-1e8c1567ae.description: A collection of solitaire games played with cards, mahjong tiles and colored panels.
pc88:local-1e8c1567ae.title: Ginga

pc88:local-207a81fdfe.description: A naval simulation: command the sailing ship Thousantis in semi-turn-based battles against other ships, and perhaps find land to go ashore.
pc88:local-207a81fdfe.title: Adventure of Thousantis

pc88:local-20b0d31cfe.description: A three-disk RPG set in a Wizardry-style wireframe dungeon where the enemies are girls, in the manner of Chaos Angels, with puzzles and events along the way and art by ASUKA.
pc88:local-20b0d31cfe.title: Extra

pc88:local-213e3f94ee.description: A 1990 Firecracker disk of minor game music, covering rarely arranged titles such as Cyber Tank and Atomic Robo-Kid; it loads PCM much faster than earlier issues and hides a 31st track that only plays when the computer's clock is set to December.
pc88:local-213e3f94ee.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 12 - Minor Game Music Special

pc88:local-216cf4302d.description: A three-disk RPG also sold on Takeru: Areos, son of a hero, travels a demon-ridden land after the sword that once sealed an ancient god, in an episodic multi-scenario story with adventure-style towns, a map for travel, and first-person battles that raise stats after every fight.
pc88:local-216cf4302d.title: S-I-V-A

pc88:local-223582517d.description: A Plotting-style puzzle game: throw the block in hand to remove matching blocks against a time limit, aiming to finish with only three blocks left.
pc88:local-223582517d.title: Flippal

pc88:local-228f7fe835.description: A card game whose title mimics Xevious: the economic control system Yyeleiss has run amok, and the player must beat its three guard computers at Nine Card, which turns out to be the Japanese game Kabu; the girl beside the table plays no part.
pc88:local-228f7fe835.title: Yyeleiss

pc88:local-23909abe74.description: A fixed-screen shooter in which a spellcaster blasts slimes and other creatures; each very different boss defeated adds a new spell to the starting fireball.
pc88:local-23909abe74.title: Devotion

pc88:local-2433618eee.description: A dating game: choose one of four women and win her over in conversation.
pc88:local-2433618eee.title: Yaritai Houdai

pc88:local-25a9edf319.description: A tile-matching puzzle in the manner of Shanghai: turn over all 136 mahjong tiles in matching pairs.
pc88:local-25a9edf319.title: Dragon

pc88:local-26df82d72b.description: A vertical shooter made with the shooting-game editor included in Tatesuka Wars.
pc88:local-26df82d72b.title: Teruru

pc88:local-2710c7fb8f.description: A demo built on the first ending song of the anime NG Knight Ramune & 40.
pc88:local-2710c7fb8f.title: Atashi no Pa Pi Pu Pe Po

pc88:local-275956cba7.description: Junichi Ueda's second music disk: arrangements from Turbo OutRun, Galaxy Force, Burning Force, The Legend of Valkyrie, Power Drift and Night Striker, a few of Ueda's own compositions, and odd covers such as the children's song Oyoge! Taiyaki-kun.
pc88:local-275956cba7.title: Ueda Junichi BGM Collection Vol. 2

pc88:local-28a9118bcf.description: Zeal Soft's 50-yen command-driven romance adventure: a schoolgirl who fell for Hiroshi after he hit her with a football as a child tries to win his heart years later.
pc88:local-28a9118bcf.title: Splash 2

pc88:local-29389b0036.description: Released alongside volume 33 in 1996, this Firecracker disk is built around the Harlem Blade soundtrack with further tracks hidden behind a keyboard trick, and was apparently the circle's last new music disk.
pc88:local-29389b0036.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 34 - Harlem Blade Recollection

pc88:local-2a870cb1c7.description: Extra scenarios for Sorcerian produced by Conrad T. Ozawa and supervised by Falcom: five adventures, among them The Two-Headed Hellhound.
pc88:local-2a870cb1c7.title: Sorcerian Tsuika Scenario - Gilgamesh Sorcerian

pc88:local-2ace156d08.description: A vertical shooter made with Tatesuka Wars' editor: choose which power-up to take from those dropped by enemies, clear the screen with wipers, and face bosses; a PC-98 sequel followed.
pc88:local-2ace156d08.title: Tokuichi Tiger

pc88:local-2b756e52be.description: A 1992 edition of NT-3's music disk Yume no Fantasia for computers without a Sound Board II: the same content on the standard FM sound, minus the game music corner, for 41 tracks.
pc88:local-2b756e52be.title: Yume no Fantasia Normal - NT-3 Music Disk

pc88:local-2be6088c6c.description: An Arkanoid-style block breaker whose ball only rebounds at 45-degree angles.
pc88:local-2be6088c6c.title: Marmalade

pc88:local-2c5fff9afa.description: A board game in the manner of Monopoly: buy up tourist spots and grow rich on the dice, with place names and chance cards you can rename and computer players who react as they play.
pc88:local-2c5fff9afa.title: American Success

pc88:local-2de00a3014.description: An election simulation: run against six other candidates through a 24-day campaign of posters, speeches and bribery, which can get you arrested, before voting day on June 30.
pc88:local-2de00a3014.title: The Senkyo

pc88:local-2e77372cee.description: A war simulation themed on the Gulf War, opening with a debt-ridden man picking a fight with a wealthy girl; the weak Kuwaiti army makes pushing back the Iraqi forces very hard.
pc88:local-2e77372cee.title: Summer Resort Chuukintou

pc88:local-2f406a13a0.description: Shogi with Kōji Tanigawa: play five opponents with their own favorite strategies, solve forty tsume-shogi problems, or pick the best next move.
pc88:local-2f406a13a0.title: Tanigawa Koji no Shougi Shinan II

pc88:local-2f918727c2.description: A doujin adventure about a band of schoolboys.
pc88:local-2f918727c2.title: Yuugekitai

pc88:local-2fa01f5cc6.title: The Continuing Story of Maru-guro Marumaru-zou

pc88:local-2fae9ca69f.description: The second Sadistic Gamers quiz from Sixteens (1990): a student struggling with his studies takes a supplementary lesson from his teacher, and answering her questions well moves the lesson along.
pc88:local-2fae9ca69f.title: Sadistic Gamers 2

pc88:local-2ffc37d2b7.description: Megafeps' third collection of original compositions (1992), bright tunes with high bell-like melodies and darker pieces driven by restless bass lines and syncopation, plus a guest track by Firecracker's CHEMOOL.
pc88:local-2ffc37d2b7.title: Music Arena Vol. 5

pc88:local-312f8c6ffb.description: A parody of the classic Star Trek strategy game, also released on the FM-7.
pc88:local-312f8c6ffb.title: Uchuu Senkan Yamato Takeru

pc88:local-318afc3e84.description: A board game for one to four players that claims to be about life but is really about spreading your color across the board, entirely at the mercy of the die.
pc88:local-318afc3e84.title: Tomita

pc88:local-32569dc182.description: ECE Software Factory, pioneers of doujin quiz games, made this 1987 quiz with graphics by NAO Graphics Lab and title music by a young Yuzo Koshiro.
pc88:local-32569dc182.title: Long Night

pc88:local-3257d1bb81.title: Area PC-88 - The Last Red Fighter

pc88:local-325b05751c.description: An adventure on a mysterious island populated mostly by young women: talk to people, examine things and wander around to learn what the island is about.
pc88:local-325b05751c.title: Bishoujo Jackal 2 - Ore no Shima

pc88:local-32aae853c8.description: A 1991 Firecracker collection of hard-edged covers from Bosconian, Actraiser, Genocide, Lagoon and The Scheme, plus a standout Night Arms arrangement, alongside one contributor's renditions of Wink and Yuki Saito pop songs.
pc88:local-32aae853c8.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 18 - Ardor for Game Music

pc88:local-32b6fa36c7.description: A block-pushing puzzle in which the player, a heart, moves blocks to steer a young woman who walks on her own toward the exit door.
pc88:local-32b6fa36c7.title: Mature

pc88:local-32c2ca5469.description: Onion Software's 1986 parody RPG in the Ultima mold: rescue a princess held deep in a dungeon, with gags throughout, cameos by other doujin circles, punishing difficulty and a hidden Majaventure picture as a bonus; it was one of the magazine-featured titles that first made doujin software known.
pc88:local-32c2ca5469.title: Harvecy

pc88:local-333938f279.description: A side-scrolling action game in which a knight rescues fairies over adventures of four levels each, with bosses guarding keys, food to restore health, and items like a magic wand, flying shoes and a harmful skull.
pc88:local-333938f279.title: Heroes

pc88:local-345c11bee4.description: Three-way rock-paper-scissors with your partner Yukari against a third girl.
pc88:local-345c11bee4.title: Bishoujo Hippagashi Game

pc88:local-34eb44de6a.description: NT-3's first music disk for Active Gamers (1990): 53 tracks, mostly NT-3's own compositions, for the standard FM sound only, with a bonus corner reached by pressing Return on the title screen.
pc88:local-34eb44de6a.title: Mysterious Love Token - NT-3 Music Disk

pc88:local-357ed50ec1.description: A fantasy adventure in which Kain, arrived from another world, travels with Myutika, whose black hair marks her as cursed in this land, to defeat the demon king.
pc88:local-357ed50ec1.title: Kurokami no Densetsu

pc88:local-35a7e8ae4e.description: Onion Software's last PC-88 release (1990), the seventh 100 Yen Disk: the all-weather shooting action game The Busy Home Town, TSUKKA Software's Space Hanazukin-chan and Creative H.A.T.'s racer Yoshio-kun Dasu P!! Mawarunda, with music from eight composers making full use of PCM.
pc88:local-35a7e8ae4e.title: 100 Yen Disk No. 7 Final

pc88:local-37a59c5a74.description: G_Club Software's 1989 action game: rotate and thrust an inertia-bound craft called the Hunter to reach the goal within the time limit, with cute girl graphics and music by KAJA.
pc88:local-37a59c5a74.title: Nukeru Master

pc88:local-382fc5f0bc.description: Swimming-loving schoolgirl Mia plans to stop at a crepe shop with her friend Eriko after school; art by Fozon.
pc88:local-382fc5f0bc.title: Take Out Vol. 5

pc88:local-38ae9b0226.description: A Tetris clone where clearing the required rows lets the player choose between the next level and a harder one.
pc88:local-38ae9b0226.title: Brash Point II

pc88:local-38c80bbbe1.description: A battle-focused, Wizardry-style 3D dungeon RPG where defeated monsters can join the party; it was distributed copy-free with an on-disk manual.
pc88:local-38c80bbbe1.title: Lion

pc88:local-395ef96b63.title: Tottemo H na Graphics 2 - Fruity Girls

pc88:local-39d5a08552.description: A very short Alice in Wonderland adventure in which Alice follows the white rabbit down the hole and the player only picks between two choices at each step.
pc88:local-39d5a08552.title: Fushigi no Kuni Gekijou

pc88:local-3a6344405b.description: An FC-Software disk of minigames including Rich Racer (collect dollar signs), a bungee jump scored on depth, a number-mashing cartwheel race and a money grab that speeds up each level.
pc88:local-3a6344405b.title: Haniriito Vol. 7

pc88:local-3a8265f6ec.description: ALU Computer Arts' 100-yen bundle of a mostly original music collection and Phrenetic Shooting, a fast fixed-screen bullet-dodging shooter that stood out when most doujin games were slow picture-story adventures.
pc88:local-3a8265f6ec.title: Phrenetic Shooting & 100 Yen Ongaku Disk

pc88:local-3c26a5bbdd.description: A dice-driven board game with RPG and strategy elements: from the starting inn, stop the rolling die, then fight, hire soldiers or even get drunk depending on the space, aiming to reach and slay the dragon.
pc88:local-3c26a5bbdd.title: Dragon Blood

pc88:local-3c74c3abf3.description: Firecracker's eleventh music collection (1990), given over almost entirely to Gofer no Yabou Episode II tunes, with CG by Akira Araki; it began using the Sound Board II's 256 KB of RAM as a RAM disk, a buggy feature that led to a second version without it.
pc88:local-3c74c3abf3.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 11 - Gofer Episode 2 Issue

pc88:local-3c9409437e.description: A two-player-only action game set in a future where war has been replaced by arena battles between tanks that can jump.
pc88:local-3c9409437e.title: Gunnerays

pc88:local-3f88451dc9.description: Third game in Scatter Brain's shooter series after Crinex, this time a vertically scrolling shooter with forgiving difficulty; an illustration follows each cleared stage, and a no-continue clear on Hard is said to change the ending.
pc88:local-3f88451dc9.title: Scottie Turbo

pc88:local-3fa6691416.description: Selected Sorcerian 2: two prize-winning scenarios from the Sorcerian scenario contest, Pandora's Box, in which the evils let out of a box must be put back, and The Scorching Trap.
pc88:local-3fa6691416.title: Sorcerian Tsuika Scenario - Selected Sorcerian 2

pc88:local-402b77dd9f.description: A puzzle game: drop playing cards into a five-by-five grid to make poker hands across its rows, columns and diagonals.
pc88:local-402b77dd9f.title: Ryukyu

pc88:local-4030ace524.description: Selected Sorcerian 1, the first of the Sorcerian scenario contest winners: The Beautiful Bride and The Town Where the Silver Light Went Out, with a magazine disk.
pc88:local-4030ace524.title: Sorcerian Tsuika Scenario - Selected Sorcerian 1

pc88:local-4068e9e83e.description: A novelty disk from Black FTZ: a yellow wire-frame Nadia figure dances all over the screen to an endlessly looping PCM recording of the 'Yashi no Mi Natera' dish-soap jingle. It was ported to the PC-88 after a warm reception on machines like the PC-98.
pc88:local-4068e9e83e.title: Tennen Yashi no Mi Natera

pc88:local-41ab0f09fc.description: Falcom's utility disk for Sorcerian: easily create any of 120 spells, rename items and characters, move characters between save disks, and shop at a store with limited stock that displays whatever you sell, plus extras such as a board game, a quiz and a music mode.
pc88:local-41ab0f09fc.title: Sorcerian System - Utility Vol. 1

pc88:local-446e51b88a.description: First of the three self-booting Amazing Disk episodes, introduced by a 'mysterious Amazing Disk' narration; this one holds Onion Software's game Box Express Flying in the Sky.
pc88:local-446e51b88a.title: Amazing Disk Episode I

pc88:local-458d267711.description: Fifth disk in Onion Software's 100 Yen Disk series, made with outside circles: Creative H.A.T.'s Fuusen, OSS's sushi puzzle and Jumper 3, the series' first Sound Board II game, with music by Yuzo Koshiro and Shinji Hosoe.
pc88:local-458d267711.title: 100 Yen Disk No. 5

pc88:local-47159519a0.description: Third disk in zeal soft's Splash series, nominally an adventure game though the author admits it barely works as one; it features mostly male characters, music by Waki, and a deliberately slack bonus quiz mode.
pc88:local-47159519a0.title: Splash 3

pc88:local-47c885c13b.description: Tsukumo's yakyuuken rock-paper-scissors game, a hit among the many versions of the time, by Tadashi Makimura (Mari-chan Kiki Ippatsu) and based on one he drew in his Shonen Magazine manga Micom Love.
pc88:local-47c885c13b.title: Yakyuuken

pc88:local-4c63068657.description: School-themed side story starring the girls of Fairie's Residence, subtitled Sailor-fuku to Hitobanjuu; like the other Specials it came with a comic that ties in with the software.
pc88:local-4c63068657.title: Fairie's Residence Special 3 - Gakuen-hen

pc88:local-4c9ce39c6f.description: Three quirky PMD music disks by zeal soft's Kamijo: vol. 1 has a free-talk corner recommending ramen shops over PCM horse-race commentary, vol. 2 a real-time scaling title screen, and vol. 3 oddly named tracks and a menu that appraises your PC-88's resale value.
pc88:local-4c9ce39c6f.title: Cone-shi Shindou Data Pack

pc88:local-4defeaa5de.title: Music Lalf - Hyper Music Macro Language

pc88:local-4e4e6a8a25.description: Second 100 Yen Disk omnibus sold at Comiket: Wincrolizeth (dive into a vortex past a boss lifted from Fantasy Zone), the image-guessing quiz Karleloa and four-player block breaker Rotten Wall Jr., the Darius-themed volleyball game Darai Ball, Jumpper II and the first Sushi Game.
pc88:local-4e4e6a8a25.title: 100 Yen Disk No. 2

pc88:local-4e77026114.title: Todo no Tsumari no H Disk

pc88:local-4e8f41f6a9.description: Orphe's fourth PC-88 music disk, first sold at Comiket 44 and made for the Sound Board II; it carries fewer tracks than earlier disks but adds a bonus game.
pc88:local-4e8f41f6a9.title: Sound Theater

pc88:local-4f1a953694.description: Third issue of Champion Soft's disk magazine Omega, containing programs such as Uketsukejou ni Attack and Osaka-jou Adventure.
pc88:local-4f1a953694.title: Omega No. 3

pc88:local-4f3a603287.description: A numbers-driven baseball simulation for one or two players: call the pitch's course, type and speed, and give detailed orders at bat and on the mound.
pc88:local-4f3a603287.title: Super Baseball Simulation

pc88:local-4fdf493dca.description: A 3D wireframe flight simulator: fly the Red Wing with ailerons, rudder and elevator, take off and land, and destroy enemy fighters, factories and the super colony's control computer.
pc88:local-4fdf493dca.title: Red Wing

pc88:local-4ffe05ffd3.description: LOGiN magazine's follow-up to Adventure Tsukuuru, the first 'Tsukuuru' maker, published in the October 1987 issue: a tool for building command-selection adventure games that adds support for pictures.
pc88:local-4ffe05ffd3.title: Adventure Tsukuuru mkII

pc88:local-500c90deec.description: A horizontally scrolling shooter programmed by ZURA, the release that launched Charlie Soft as a doujin circle.
pc88:local-500c90deec.title: Sigma

pc88:local-511844f9fd.description: Princess Mefilia of planet Pure, destroyed by planet Gear, joins the army of planet Utia to take revenge and uncovers one conspiracy after another in this three-part science-fiction adventure on six disks; wrong commands mean instant death.
pc88:local-511844f9fd.title: Bulena

pc88:local-5142735591.description: A fantasy adventure with unusual automapping, built as a campaign system: later scenario disks such as Oono-san Panic and Ninja Keisatsu run on the same engine.
pc88:local-5142735591.title: Meikyuu Roman

pc88:local-5142a09799.description: A two-disk PMD music collection from Exiz, mainly new pieces from an RPG and from Dragon Star, including Denshou, which drops voice samples into its rhythm over a driving bass line.
pc88:local-5142a09799.title: Exiz Music Disk Vol. II - The Power Live

pc88:local-5180cd9c16.description: A hero convinced he is a gambling genius sets out to conquer the world, loses at poker to a girl in a bar, and learns a huge gambling syndicate stands behind her. Color poker duels use life gauges and usable items.
pc88:local-5180cd9c16.title: Discard

pc88:local-525450aeb8.description: Firecracker's ninth music disk, a small feature on Akumajou Densetsu and Ys music, with a Dirt Fox track crammed into about 13 KB, Kuuga (later bundled with PMD as a sample) and an original by Hacker magazine contributor Yoshinori Mori.
pc88:local-525450aeb8.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 09 - Arrange Version Issue

pc88:local-529fbd912e.description: Second in Lolita Soft's gentle fairy-tale adventure series about Sayoko, with a story of girlish sentiment like the first; the single-color graphics come from its move to 400-line mode.
pc88:local-529fbd912e.title: Sayoko 2

pc88:local-5328d40756.description: Firecracker's seventh music disk, the first to switch to the PMD driver and to use PCM samples, and the first to add illustrations, establishing the screen layout the series kept from then on.
pc88:local-5328d40756.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 07 - SB2 Full Power!! In PMD

pc88:local-53d423428c.description: Third in SSL and Peach Land's card game series, an RPG-flavored game with only four card types: cards are turned up by luck, attack cards reveal more of the picture according to their strength, and monsters cost hit points.
pc88:local-53d423428c.title: Card Force 3

pc88:local-5441baff28.description: The first sample disk for FSD, Frostforest's very compact FM music driver for the PC-88, running on their large FROST-DOS, with tracks by MKR, Monden, yon", Osamu Ishikawa, Active Gamers' NT-3 and SHYNER.
pc88:local-5441baff28.title: FSD Sample Ongaku Shuu Vol. 1

pc88:local-5487435e63.description: A two-disk picture gallery: a skeletal host welcomes the visitor to his 'mansion of demon girls' far from the human world, after which around sixteen pictures of its girls by manga artist Senno Knife are shown; there is essentially no game.
pc88:local-5487435e63.title: Senno Knife no Mashoujokan

pc88:local-563034addc.description: A 1991 digest collection of Fairytale's games sold only through the TAKERU software vending machines, including a digest version of Lipstick Adventure 2.
pc88:local-563034addc.title: Fairytale Kaizokuban

pc88:local-577bd9d604.description: Junichi Ueda's second music collection from PSG Soft, with arrangements from Turbo OutRun, Burning Force, Valkyrie no Densetsu and Night Striker, several Ueda originals and odd covers such as Oyoge! Taiyaki-kun; the '+' edition gives the originals titles.
pc88:local-577bd9d604.title: Ueda Junichi BGM Collection Vol. 2+

pc88:local-579183d0c6.description: A best-of disk from the music circle Orphe that packs the disk with its original and game music, centered on Hasegawa's compositions and opened by a striking logo effect; it was sold at Comiket 43 to 46 in slightly revised editions.
pc88:local-579183d0c6.title: Orphe Music Best

pc88:local-58e0335cc1.description: A poker variant played with seven kinds of illustrated cards, seven of each, so hands get their own names such as 'Only You' and 'Sister'; points earned change the large on-screen picture of the opponent.
pc88:local-58e0335cc1.title: Hunter Card

pc88:local-58f4c3a2ea.description: A fill-in-the-blank adventure in the style of HARD's Kindo Gals: hidden words in the text must be replaced by a word of the right length to win the girl over. This volume features 15-year-old schoolgirl Asuka Kato, a gym committee member who is bad at sports.
pc88:local-58f4c3a2ea.title: Take Out Vol. 1

pc88:local-596fcae3ba.description: The final chapter of Tsukka Software's Spirit series of field-map RPGs, an unusually large doujin release on eight disks with music by CHOBIN; only the opening demo uses ADPCM, and a hidden alternate opening is included.
pc88:local-596fcae3ba.title: D.K.

pc88:local-598faad68e.description: A science-fiction adventure: a crew sent to survey ruins left by aliens runs into a mysterious radar image, a swarm of asteroids and a girl caught up in a dimensional rift, with mini-games along the way.
pc88:local-598faad68e.title: Remembrance

pc88:local-59ad2c7d71.description: A parody of DB-Soft's Konya mo Asa made Powerful Mahjong played as rock-paper-scissors against three girls, with one or two hidden opponents.
pc88:local-59ad2c7d71.title: Powerful Janken EXE

pc88:local-59f5a88433.description: First of four side stories starring the girls of Fairie's Residence, subtitled Mariko no Ikenai Daitokkun; it came with a comic that ties in with the software.
pc88:local-59f5a88433.title: Fairie's Residence Special 1 - Club-hen

pc88:local-5af36afec6.description: A detective adventure: a school detective club looks into the case of a runaway student.
pc88:local-5af36afec6.title: Tanteidan X

pc88:local-5bf590e48b.description: Third Phrenetic Shooting from ALU Computer Arts, a dodging-focused shooter with even denser enemy fire than before and bosses for the first time; every enemy shot down is worth just one point.
pc88:local-5bf590e48b.title: Phrenetic Shooting - Third Mission

pc88:local-5c4ceeccc2.description: Firecracker's 19th music disk, highlighted by Mishima's Sound Board II arrangement of Revolter, a small Yuzo Koshiro feature and originals by Ishikawa and Monden, plus Junko Ozawa's Standard Theme; the cover art is by Kenichi Minoda.
pc88:local-5c4ceeccc2.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 19 - Increase Activity!

pc88:local-5c545f7179.description: Selected Sorcerian 4: The Goddess Who Vanished into Darkness, the contest's only scenario by a woman, and the Chinese-flavored Youmugen Legend with jiangshi and pandas.
pc88:local-5c545f7179.title: Sorcerian Tsuika Scenario - Selected Sorcerian 4

pc88:local-5de0852c85.description: A computer version of jankyuu, the mahjong-themed pinball-style parlor game, offering three machines and two-player play; developed by Coconuts 21 for Victor's CrossMedia Soft label.
pc88:local-5de0852c85.title: Jang Ball

pc88:local-5ef27a06bd.description: A score-attack shooter from Firecracker: score as much as possible within two minutes. Results differ by machine speed and Sound Board II presence, and a replay mode feeds the per-model rankings printed in Firecracker's music disks.
pc88:local-5ef27a06bd.title: Super Sonic Shooter

pc88:local-5fe26392e7.description: Firecracker's 22nd music disk and its second CHEMOOL originals special, dressed in Kazuhiko Shimamoto-style hot-blooded art and built around music for the mahjong game Tekken Seisai, Nouten Chokugeki! 3 and CG collections from KDD and D-TEN.
pc88:local-5fe26392e7.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 22 - Iron Gear Issue

pc88:local-606b58458f.description: A word game: as Kazuki Kuremoto, win girls over with words alone by picking the right replies; wrong answers make you drink milk until the game ends.
pc88:local-606b58458f.title: Ikase Otoko Nyuumon - Ai o Arigatou

pc88:local-6098c418fa.description: An adventure combined with a stage-clearing puzzle game on four disks; booting from the PCM disk with a Sound Board II makes the birds and the girl speak, and a puzzle construction mode is included.
pc88:local-6098c418fa.title: Beed

pc88:local-61aa0d4504.title: Game Music Collection Vol. 1 - Sega & Draque II

pc88:local-61f5bf743e.description: An animated crossword game with eight bunny girls and fiendishly hard puzzles.
pc88:local-61f5bf743e.title: Bunny-chan no Himitsu

pc88:local-62d2be5fcf.description: An RPG starring an ordinary slime who answers the king's call for heroes after Princess Imu of Slime Land is kidnapped by an evil sorcerer; the game bills itself as made for a mental age of 12 and under.
pc88:local-62d2be5fcf.title: Slime Land Story

pc88:local-64ac59e131.description: A doujin adventure: the lively student Morina is having a busy day as usual when she finds herself in a mysterious world.
pc88:local-64ac59e131.title: Morina

pc88:local-650148c957.description: Specters' take on Mastermind: deduce the hidden code by trial guesses, which a little logic cracks in a handful of tries, making it a quick break between longer games.
pc88:local-650148c957.title: Brunette

pc88:local-652a230891.description: A collection of four-panel comics starring Miki from Champion Soft's disk magazine Zeta, with parts of some panels animated.
pc88:local-652a230891.title: Ganbare! Miki-chan

pc88:local-669628406a.description: A side story to Yuugekitai: a submarine suddenly appears off the coast, and the squad returns to uncover its secrets.
pc88:local-669628406a.title: Yuugekitai Bangaihen

pc88:local-66af29c47a.title: Oyama no Taishou Music Collection Vol. 2 - The Best Selection Arrange-hen

pc88:local-66fcce00b7.description: ASCII's construction kit for horizontally scrolling shooters (the name puns on 'yoko scroll'): draw the player ship, enemies and backgrounds, pick the music and set enemy movement patterns to build your own game. Sold through TAKERU vending machines around 1988.
pc88:local-66fcce00b7.title: Yokosuka Wars

pc88:local-6762fa6299.description: Tsukka Software's first release, a two-disk field-map RPG from 1987 that began the Spirit series, continued in Umi no Mukou (Spirit 2) and concluded with the eight-disk Dragon Knights.
pc88:local-6762fa6299.title: Spirit

pc88:local-682c16a63d.description: Firecracker's 16th music disk, given over to CHEMOOL's own compositions, including music written for doujin releases such as Tetra Force and Hanayaide Osaka, plus a hidden patch fixing a track from the previous issue.
pc88:local-682c16a63d.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 16 - Original Music Special

pc88:local-682f623b30.description: As a new teacher at a girls' school, you are infatuated with student Kumiko and must fend off the other schoolgirls while trying to arrange private after-school lessons with her.
pc88:local-682f623b30.title: Hime Ringo Report

pc88:local-692c1ca51d.description: First issue of Champion Soft's 'graphic idol magazine' Zeta, a disk sold with a printed magazine that created fictional idols and presented their profiles and pin-up pictures, along with some games.
pc88:local-692c1ca51d.title: Zeta No. 1

pc88:local-69f28649e9.description: A blackjack game against a fiercely strong computer, ported from Iron Gear's X68000 and MSX2 versions by Firecracker's AQUA under the Mad Pierrot name, with Sound Board II music and pictures that scroll across two full screens.
pc88:local-69f28649e9.title: Nouten Chokugeki II

pc88:local-6a9348e87e.description: Show-business side story starring the girls of Fairie's Residence, subtitled Super Mariko Sisters and played as a sugoroku-style board game; it came with a tie-in comic.
pc88:local-6a9348e87e.title: Fairie's Residence Special 4 - Geinoukai-hen

pc88:local-6af4b781a2.description: A war simulation of the Battle of the Coral Sea: lead up to four fleets toward Port Moresby against the American fleet in semi-real time, never knowing the enemy's losses until the end.
pc88:local-6af4b781a2.title: Kuubo Kidou Butai

pc88:local-6b731819f9.description: A panel-sliding puzzle like a pipe game: a bunny shifts whole rows or columns of 24 wrap-around panels to link the start and goal panels within a limited number of moves.
pc88:local-6b731819f9.title: Tomo-chan Ganbaru

pc88:local-6d82d2cd53.description: A 100-yen pack of four bizarre games from Ayashige Soft, including two 'Miyamo' games, a moxibustion game using the members' own relatives as material, and a fashion contest.
pc88:local-6d82d2cd53.title: Ayashige Pack

pc88:local-6dcb106ed4.description: A Bomberman-style action puzzle for one or two players: set off the bombs scattered around the field in chain reactions to drain the opponent's endurance to zero. Simple rules hide a lot of strategy, and the explosion animation is elaborate.
pc88:local-6dcb106ed4.title: Explode

pc88:local-6df7f2739c.description: A parody of Little Red Riding Hood: sent by her mother to visit her grandmother, she faces traps all along the way.
pc88:local-6df7f2739c.title: Akazukin-chan

pc88:local-6f39223cd3.description: A comic show-business adventure on three disks: newly hired at TKO Production, you are ordered to scout new idol Yonami Watanabe and make her a top star. The title screen uses a photo of Minayo Watanabe.
pc88:local-6f39223cd3.title: Kare to Futari no Skyline

pc88:local-6f801134ae.description: Third music disk from Yanbaru Kuina, with illustrations by Fox and a very fast custom DOS by K-na that adds striking visual effects to the tracks.
pc88:local-6f801134ae.title: Sound On-Ten Vol. 3

pc88:local-6f9b24f378.description: Music software for the PC-8801's Sound Board II, supervised by Koichi Sugiyama, with sample arrangements included.
pc88:local-6f9b24f378.title: Formula C.M.S.

pc88:local-7090d58fcc.title: Rama Software 100 Yen Music Disk Vol. 1

pc88:local-70df9f50d9.description: A science-fiction adventure set in 2552: find the weakness of the alien Danak to save the colony planet Farras.
pc88:local-70df9f50d9.title: Time Secret

pc88:local-71069a4604.description: Second of the three self-booting Amazing Disk episodes, holding OSS's game Jinsei no Katachi (The Shape of Life).
pc88:local-71069a4604.title: Amazing Disk Episode II

pc88:local-72b5843706.description: A song-themed adventure from Active Gamers (August 1991) played with RPG-style top-down movement in the manner of The Old Village Story; the NT-3 music disk Mysterious Love Token 98 came with it as a bonus.
pc88:local-72b5843706.title: Inifinitia

pc88:local-740abcad30.description: The fourth FSD sample music disk from Frostforest, celebrating Chaikuro joining the circle with his originals across many genres, including pieces written for the X68000 RPG Kaze no Tabibito and a hardcore techno track built on orchestra hits.
pc88:local-740abcad30.title: FSD Sample Ongaku Shuu Vol. 4

pc88:local-74a234ab16.description: Sixth volume of Marionet's Take Out fill-in-the-blank adventures, in which a boy visits a café whose waitresses wear sailor uniforms.
pc88:local-74a234ab16.title: Take Out Vol. 6

pc88:local-75543c5958.description: Charlie Soft's first music disk, played through the PC/M88 driver with its distinctive SSG sound: mostly original tunes plus rarely heard picks such as the battle music from Sangokushi and the opening of Jesus.
pc88:local-75543c5958.title: Charlie Soft Music Disk Vol. 1

pc88:local-7656e5ebb2.description: A doujin adventure: a girl gives the hero a key, and that night a mysterious dream begins.
pc88:local-7656e5ebb2.title: SD Toki no Kagi

pc88:local-76beaf6729.description: Chosen to play the fugitive in a WASP special police training drill, you must escape a 3D maze generated anew each time, armed only with a stun gun and a Star Blade while nine teammates hunt you; stats come from an Ultima IV-style personality quiz.
pc88:local-76beaf6729.title: Tiny Wasp

pc88:local-787477e14c.description: A Team Dangeroude music disk running on FROST-DOS with the FSD driver, including Puyo Puyo music and another essay by Yamazaki.
pc88:local-787477e14c.title: Con Spirito

pc88:local-79375663c5.description: A chess game with four levels, saved games, and a problem mode of mate-in-three puzzles.
pc88:local-79375663c5.title: Chess-IV

pc88:local-7a3b474127.description: A doujin adventure: win the heroine Milady, with many encounters along the way.
pc88:local-7a3b474127.title: Sweet Girl

pc88:local-7a9eddf314.description: First game in Kankyouken's Aya-chan series, known for its distinctive cute art: an adventure with a rather harsh scenario told at a leisurely pace.
pc88:local-7a9eddf314.title: Aya-chan Suplex

pc88:local-7c9212e048.description: Kurosawa's world-scale strategy game for Camadamia Soft (1990), built around pointed profiles of the world's dangerous leaders, written before the Gulf War yet seeming to foresee it; it is the only game to use zeal soft Kamijo's sound driver.
pc88:local-7c9212e048.title: Rule the World

pc88:local-7cfec59cec.description: A singing disk on which Karasawa plays guitar and belts out Tsuyoshi Nagabuchi's Doshaburi Rainy Day, played back as PCM synthesized through the PSG.
pc88:local-7cfec59cec.title: Kimochi Disk 2 - Karasawa-kun no Uta

pc88:local-7d2a360d88.description: A free disk Active Gamers handed out in August 1992 to mark two years since forming, recording the circle's history and even including a glossary of its in-jokes and terms.
pc88:local-7d2a360d88.title: 2nd Anniversary Disk

pc88:local-7ee53fbbca.description: Part IV of Oak's Fantastic Cubic line, a three-dimensional color-matching puzzle developed by Kyoto Computer Brains and released in 1983.
pc88:local-7ee53fbbca.title: Twenty by Twelve - Fantastic Cubic Game

pc88:local-804fe7c10a.description: TSUKKA software's event disk for Comic Market 41, named after NEC's Bazaar de Gozaru mascot: a board-game quiz and a racing game with text-based scaling and rotation, full PCM voices and a music room for Chobin's tunes.
pc88:local-804fe7c10a.title: Fuyu de Gozaaru

pc88:local-80aa019898.description: Active Gamers' second 100-yen extra disk (1992), packed with a rejected scenario from their game Infinitia, a music collection and a complete walkthrough of Holiness Story.
pc88:local-80aa019898.title: Extra Disk Vol. 2

pc88:local-80baa19ac4.description: First volume of Pasoket's own Kagai Jugyou series, an idol-themed multiple-choice quiz with pictures of pretty girls, made by Nihon Art Media for the label of the doujin software fair organizer and released on four disks in 1989.
pc88:local-80baa19ac4.title: Kagai Jugyou Vol. 1 - Idol-hen

pc88:local-81109b62c9.description: Sequel to Burivary System's futuristic blackjack game Medal Jack, needing the first disk to play; the rules stay the same while the girls are new.
pc88:local-81109b62c9.title: Medal Jack 2

pc88:local-81842b4b52.description: One of Firecracker's first five music disks, released together at 200 yen each and written in BASIC MML for Sound Board II.
pc88:local-81842b4b52.title: Firecracker Music Collection Vol. 05 - S.B.2 BASIC Excellents

pc88:local-8359f7ed21.description: A 20-stage puzzle game like Flappy: guide a witch pushing blocks until the light-blue block reaches the goal, using items that flip gravity and magnets that pull blocks.
pc88:local-8359f7ed21.title: Witch's Brains

pc88:local-837968b3a6.description: A card game packed with parodies that runs on a fake operating system called Humen8.8K: win money at poker and blackjack, then gather items for an RPG-style battle against a boss.
pc88:local-837968b3a6.title: Card Game Pro 8.8K Vol. 2

pc88:local-83d0a93346.description: A war game of World War II in Europe, North Africa and Arabia from the invasion of Poland to 1945: one to five players command six great powers' land, sea and air forces in three-month turns.
pc88:local-83d0a93346.title: Dai 3 Teikoku

pc88:local-840e8708b9.description: A doujin music disk compiled by Macha, playing tracks from Nihon Falcom's action RPGs Ys and Ys II on the PC-88's FM sound.
pc88:local-840e8708b9.title: Music Loud Vol. 1++

pc88:local-8447e170eb.title: Indo no Ohimesama - Kabocha Batake de Otsukimi 2
